name: Language Models can Solve Computer Tasks (RCI)
authors: Geunwoo Kim, Pierre Baldi, Stephen McAleer (UC Irvine; CMU)
venue: NeurIPS 2023 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36)
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique (Recursively Criticize and Improve, RCI): the LLM is prompted to find problems with its own output, then improve it based on that self-generated critique; for computer-control tasks RCI is applied sequentially to task-grounding, state-grounding, and agent-grounding)
feedback_source: self-generated (the model criticizes its own output with implicit prompts such as 'Review your previous answer and find problems with your answer'); for the natural-language reasoning experiments an optional external ground-truth/environment feedback signal is used to terminate the loop (max 2 RCI loops, stop when output matches ground-truth)
iteration_structure: iterative-refine (single critique-then-improve loop that can be repeated until a stopping condition: environment feedback, a maximum predetermined number of iterations, or a heuristic; for computer tasks RCI is applied step-by-step across the three grounding stages, with the state-grounding critique needed only once)
reflection_object: output content and reasoning chain / action plan: for computer tasks RCI revises the high-level natural-language plan (task grounding), the mapping to actual HTML elements (state grounding), and the executable keyboard/mouse action (agent grounding); for reasoning tasks RCI revises the answer/reasoning. No weights, no persisted memory, no code/architecture are modified.
learning_locus: in_context_verbal (pure prompting scheme; pre-trained LLM with no parameter/weight updates; 2-3 demonstrations placed in the prompt for in-context learning)
requires_training: none (zero-shot/few-shot prompting; no fine-tuning, no RL, no parameter updates; 2-3 in-context demonstrations per task only)
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge (the same LLM generates the critique of its own output); no trained reward model; for reasoning tasks an optional ground-truth/verifiable signal can terminate the loop
distillation_target: none (reflection is consumed within the inference loop and not distilled into any reusable artifact such as memory, skills, rules, or weights)
emergent_vs_engineered: prompt/scaffold-engineered: the recursive critique-and-improve behavior is induced entirely by hand-designed prompts (explicit RCI inserts a critique into the prompt; implicit RCI updates the output directly), not RL-emergent
memory_type: short-term/scratchpad (the current output, self-critique, and improved output are kept within the prompt context during the RCI loop); no long-term or episodic memory across tasks
memory_persistence: within-episode (state held only during a single task's inference loop; nothing persists across episodes, tasks, or sessions)
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a (no persistent memory store; the loop simply overwrites/replaces the previous output with the improved one within the context window)
error_localization_granularity: step-level and response-level: for computer tasks RCI corrects errors per grounding step (task/state/agent grounding) and per action in the plan; for reasoning tasks it critiques and revises the holistic answer/reasoning chain
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task (refinement happens within a single task/episode via the critique-improve loop; no experience is transferred across tasks, unlike Reflexion/ExpeL)
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: mid-trajectory-recovery / post-hoc-revision within the same episode: RCI improves the plan and each action before/at execution time; it is a within-task self-correction rather than cross-episode avoidance
task_domains: web/computer GUI navigation (keyboard and mouse control of computer tasks) plus general QA/reasoning (arithmetic and commonsense natural-language reasoning)
benchmarks: MiniWoB++ (computer-control); plus 8 reasoning datasets across arithmetic and commonsense following Kojima et al. (e.g., GSM8K, AddSub, SingleEq, CommonSenseQA, StrategyQA)
headline_result: On MiniWoB++ with InstructGPT-3+RLHF (gpt-3.5-turbo), RCI achieves the second-highest average success rate among all baselines (behind only CC-Net, which relies on dictionary-based typing), scoring ~41% higher than the supervised WebN-T5-3B while using fewer than 2-3 in-context demonstrations per task (vs 12K-2.4M demonstrations for SL/RL baselines) and no task-specific reward function; RCI is state-of-the-art among LLM/few-shot methods on MiniWoB++.
baselines: Computer tasks: CC-Net (SL+RL behavior cloning, 2.4M demos / 23,076 per task), WebN-T5-3B (12K-demo fine-tuned T5), other SL and RL approaches, and prior LLM agents. Reasoning: standard prompting, Few-Shot-CoT (Wei et al.), Zero-Shot-CoT (Kojima et al. 'Let's think step by step'), and ReAct/Reflexion-style references.
gains_vs_baseline: MiniWoB++: ~41% higher average success rate than WebN-T5-3B (12K demos); outperforms RL approaches that need an order of magnitude more environment interactions; second-highest overall (only CC-Net, with dictionary-based actions, is higher; vs the appropriate generative comparison CC-Net-without-dictionary, RCI is competitive). Reasoning: RCI+CoT beats CoT or RCI alone; RCI improves performance even on a 175B InstructGPT-3+RLHF model and even helps simple/commonsense tasks (e.g., CommonSenseQA, StrategyQA) where Few-Shot-CoT showed gains only at PaLM-540B scale.
compute_cost_profile: Inference-only multiplier: each task requires extra LLM calls for the critique and improvement steps (explicit RCI = at least one extra critique sample plus one improvement sample per grounding step / loop), applied across task/state/agent grounding and capped by a maximum number of RCI loops (e.g., max 2 loops in the reasoning experiments). No training/gradient cost; cost grows with number of grounding steps and loop iterations.
known_limitations: Evaluated mainly on InstructGPT-3+RLHF (gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4), so generalization to other LLMs is unexplored; struggles with lengthy/extensive HTML states due to limited context length (pruning HTML is non-trivial); action space restricted mainly to clicks and typing, limiting web navigation; short-term decision focus overlooks long-term strategy for coordinated multi-step tasks; intricate modern UI components are hard to fully understand from HTML alone, motivating additional input modalities. For reasoning, the authors note the RCI loop is prone to false-negative critiques without an external (ground-truth) feedback mechanism.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: Mixed by domain. Computer tasks: intrinsic self-verify (implicit feedback only, no oracle label) and optional environment-execution signal. Reasoning tasks: depends on oracle-label/ground-truth to terminate the loop — the authors explicitly state that without this external feedback mechanism the RCI process is prone to false-negative critiques. This makes it a partial example of the Huang/Kamoi 'self-correction needs external signal' critique.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent / partly requires-oracle: net-positive for computer-control grounding using only implicit self-feedback; for natural-language reasoning the reported gains rely on a ground-truth stopping criterion (max 2 loops, stop when output matches the label), and the authors note false-negative critiques arise without that external signal.
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper does not report calibration/confidence metrics or a 'reasoning tax'; it focuses on task success rate and reasoning accuracy)
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (RCI is a self-correction/prompting method, not a failure-attribution system; it identifies and fixes problems in its own output but does not produce a failure-mode taxonomy or attribute failures to agents/steps in a formal benchmark sense)
failure_mode_addressed: Targets logical/reasoning errors in the model's own answers (e.g., overlooked terms in arithmetic) and action-grounding errors in computer tasks (task-inappropriate, state-infeasible, or non-admissible actions); two observed agent failure modes are unexecutable actions and task failure. Relative to MAST-style modes, it most directly addresses superficial/incomplete reasoning and action-grounding errors via explicit self-critique.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new benchmark released; evaluation uses the existing MiniWoB++ benchmark and standard reasoning datasets. The authors release code (rci-agent) at https://github.com/posgnu/rci-agent.
builds_on: Self-critique / self-correction prompting (Saunders et al. self-critiquing; Ganguli et al. moral self-correction; Welleck et al. self-correct), Self-Refine (Madaan et al., iterative aspect-based self-feedback refinement), Chain-of-Thought (Wei et al.) and Zero-Shot-CoT (Kojima et al.), ReAct (Yao et al., reason+act interleaving), and the MiniWoB / MiniWoB++ web-agent benchmark (Shi et al.; Liu et al.).
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited by and contrasted with Reflexion-style and later self-reflective LLM-agent work; inspired follow-up zero-shot LLM computer-control agents (e.g., 'A Zero-Shot Language Agent for Computer Control with Structured Reflection') and broader self-correction/self-refinement literature for web/computer-use agents; frequently cited as a core training-free verbal self-refinement baseline.
reasoning_model_native: no / pre-dates reasoning models: RCI was designed for InstructGPT-3+RLHF and GPT-3.5/GPT-4-class models without built-in reflection; it externally scaffolds the critique-improve behavior rather than relying on a native reasoning model (o1/R1-style). Its premise (explicitly prompting for self-critique) overlaps with what reasoning models later internalize.
on_policy_distillation_link: none / not applicable: RCI performs no distillation and no on-policy training; it is a pure inference-time prompting loop with no skill-optimization or weight transfer, so there is no direct link to on-policy distillation.
sample_efficiency: Extremely demonstration-efficient: fewer than 2-3 in-context demonstrations per task (vs ~23,076 per task for CC-Net and 12,000 total for WebN-T5-3B) and no fine-tuning. Iteration-efficient: a small number of RCI loops (e.g., max 2 loops in the reasoning experiments; state-grounding critique applied only once for computer tasks).
